page_title: Writing a FUSE Filesystem: a Tutorial

summary.title: Writing a FUSE Filesystem: a Tutorial
summary.one_liner: You learn how to write a Filesystem in User Space (FUSE) by building a simple logging passthrough filesystem, "Big Brother File System" (BBFS), that forwards each file operation to an underlying directory.
takeaways: FUSE lets you implement file operations like open(), read() and write() in user-space code so mounted filesystems call your program.
The tutorial builds BBFS, a filesystem that passes every operation through to an underlying directory while logging it.
Example FUSE filesystems mentioned include SSHFS (remote access), jmtpfs (MTP devices) and id3fs (directories from MP3 tags).
The tutorial assumes Linux and C familiarity, with the example code in src/bbfs.c derived from fuse.h prototypes.
summary.summary: The author, Joseph Pfeiffer, presents a tutorial on writing FUSE filesystems, noting that many resources explain installing FUSE but few explain how to write one. The tutorial uses a sample filesystem called Big Brother File System (BBFS), which passes every operation to an underlying directory and logs it. The tutorial, with its code, is distributed as a tarball containing html, src and example directories. It is aimed at Linux developers comfortable with tarballs and Makefiles, and it focuses on FUSE-specific details.
